title: familiar values type not dropdown
rule: Highly familiar/predictable values → type, not dropdown.

citation.source: NN/g — Does Your Form Really Need a Dropdown List?

pass_when: Familiar/predictable values (e.g. name-like known strings) are typed.
fail_when: Those values are only in a dropdown.
overview: Highly familiar or predictable values should be typed, not dropdown-only.
apply_when: Collecting familiar predictable values like known name-like strings.
not_when: Familiar predictable values offered only inside a dropdown.
agent_hint: Prefer typing for familiar predictable values; do not lock them in dropdowns.
description: Highly familiar or predictable values belong in a type-in field, not a dropdown-only control. Users already know strings such as their own name-like values and can enter them faster by typing. Pass when familiar or predictable values are typed. Fail when those values appear only in a dropdown, forcing list hunting for content the person already knows.
